sentences.text:
By way of present petition under Section 439(2) read with Section 482 of the Code of Criminal
Procedure, 1973 ('Cr.P.C.'), the petitioner/complainant seeks cancellation of bail granted to the
respondent/accused vide order dated 18.08.2020 by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-05,
Central, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi in case arising out of Fir bearing no. 73/2020 registered under
Section 376 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 ('Ipc') at Police Station Paharganj, New Delhi on
21.03.2020.

2.  Briefly stated, the facts of the present case are that the complainant had alleged that the accused,
a resident of Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh, had come in contact with her through Facebook a year ago and they had started having conversations with each other on mobile phone.

It was alleged that on 12.10.2019, the accused had taken the complainant to a hotel and had established physical relations with her forcefully without her consent.

It was alleged that again on 30.10.2019,
the accused had established physical relations with the complainant on false pretext of marriage and when the complainant had asked the accused to get married to her, he had refused to do so and had Ms C vs State & Anr on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12453983/
1 also threatened to defame the complainant in case she disclosed about the incident to anyone.
The present FIR came to be registered on 21.03.2020 after the accused had again denied to get married to her on 26.01.2020.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner/complainant seeks setting aside of the impugned order on the ground that the learned ASJ erred in granting bail to the accused on hyper technical grounds and without appreciating the gravity of the offence.
It is stated that the investigation of the case was underway at the time of hearing of bail application and the accused had remained in judicial custody merely for a period of 45 days.

It is also stated that the complainant did not get any opportunity to show the incriminating material which had come on record by way of filing of chargesheet since the bail had already been granted to the accused before the same could be done.
4. Learned counsel for the respondent no. 2/accused, on the other hand, argues that the accused has been falsely implicated in the present case with oblique and ulterior motives.

It is stated that the accused was arrested in the present case on 04.07.2020 and after completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet, he was granted regular bail on merits by the learned ASJ on 18.08.2020 after considering the entire facts, circumstances and material on

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 17:08:34 record.

It is stated that the prosecution as well as the complainant were provided sufficient opportunity to oppose the bail application of the accused which is also evident from the submissions of the parties recorded in the impugned order.

It is, thus, stated that there is no infirmity with the impugned order and it is also contended that since the passing of impugned order, about 3 years have already passed and no adverse report has come on record regarding the accused and the accused has not violated any of the conditions which were imposed upon him by the learned ASJ while granting bail.
5.
This Court has heard arguments addressed by either side and has perused the impugned order and material on record.

6. Since the petitioner/complainant primarily seeks setting aside of order granting bail on the ground that the same was passed by taking into account irrelevant considerations and without appreciating the gravity of offence, it will be apposite to consider the law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in this regard.

In Deepak Yadav v. State of Uttar Pradesh and Anr. (2022) 8 SCC 559, the Hon'ble Apex Court had discussed the circumstances where the bail granted to an accused can be cancelled on grounds of order granting bail being perverse.

entities.text: Deepak Yadav v. State of Uttar Pradesh and Anr. (2022) 8 SCC 559
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant observations in this regard read as under:
"31.
It is no doubt true that cancellation of bail cannot be limited to the occurrence of supervening circumstances.
This Court certainly has the inherent powers and discretion to cancel the bail of an accused even in the absence of supervening circumstances.

Following are the illustrative circumstances where the bail can be cancelled:-

2
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 17:08:34 a) Where the court granting bail takes into account irrelevant material of substantial nature and not trivial nature while ignoring relevant material on record.

b) Where the court granting bail overlooks the influential position of the accused in comparison to the victim of abuse or the witnesses especially when there is prima facie misuse of position and power over the victim.
c) Where the past criminal record and conduct of the accused is completely ignored while granting bail.
d) Where bail has been granted on untenable grounds.
e) Where serious discrepancies are found in the order granting bail thereby causing prejudice to justice.
f) Where the grant of bail was not appropriate in the first place given the very serious nature of the charges against the accused which disentitles him for bail and thus cannot be justified.
g) When the order granting bail is apparently whimsical, capricious and perverse in the facts of the given case..."

7. In the present case, a perusal of impugned order dated 18.08.2020 reveals that the learned ASJ had enlarged the accused/respondent no. 2 on regular bail after taking note of the fact that the complainant in her initial complaint which had resulted in registration of FIR had alleged that the accused had made physical relations with her forcibly without her consent on 12.10.2019, however,
she in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. had stated that she had met accused for the first time on 30.05.2019 and thereafter on 30.10.2019, physical relations were established between her and the accused were with her consent, though the same had been obtained on false pretext of marriage.

It was further noted that the complainant was a 27 years old and the fact that the investigation qua accused was complete, chargesheet had already been filed and the accused was in custody since 06.07.2020.
It was also observed that the accused had no criminal This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 17:08:35 antecedents and that the trial was going to take sufficiently long time to resume and conclude in view of the outbreak of COVID-19 pandemic.

Ms C vs State & Anr on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12453983/
3 8.
In the opinion of this Court, the order granting bail to the accused does not suffer from any infirmities and no irrelevant considerations have been taken into account by the learned ASJ.

Also,
there is no gainsaying that an order granting bail cannot be construed to have any bearing on the merits of a case during the trial which is conducted and concluded as per law on the basis of detailed examination of evidence on record.

9. Moreover, about 2 years and 9 months have elapsed from the date of passing of impugned order and it is also not the case of petitioner or prosecution that the accused had flouted any of the conditions which were imposed upon him while enlarging him on bail.
10. In view of the foregoing discussion, there are no grounds to interfere with the impugned order.
11. Accordingly, the present petition stands dismissed.
12. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J MAY 19, 2023/
